title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical errors on this page. I checked (7) by direct computation: σ^{-1} = (-1/v)[[1-w,1],[v,0]], giving ρσ^{-1} = -[[1,0],[1,1]] and σ^{-1}ρ = -[[1,1/v],[0,1]]. Formulas (7bis), (9) and (11) also check out.
The condition (4) on the previous page, as transcribed ('v w' = 0, w w' = 1'), is inconsistent with (4bis) and (9). It must read v + v' = 0, w + w' = 1.

ideas.what: Normal form over an arbitrary base S for pairs (ρ, σ) in a form of PGL2 with ρσ^{-1} regular unipotent and transverse conjugate unipotent. The moduli is given by v ∈ G_m and w ∈ A^1, with a unique trivialisation of the form G.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification / representability of a moduli scheme of generator pairs of PSL2(Z)-type representations in forms of PGL2 (character-variety type normal form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical normal forms for SL2 generators (Fricke–Klein); relative versions are folklore
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche discusses SL2(Z) and the modular triangle informally; this precise normal form is unpublished as far as I know.

ideas.what: The identity σ + ρ = idempotent N, and Tr(ρ+σ) = 1, as a structural feature of modular triples
ideas.modern_name: Elementary matrix identity attached to the PSL2(Z) presentation

deep.surprise_reason: Routine, correct matrix computations establishing a relative normal form for PSL2(Z)-type generator pairs in twisted forms of PGL2. The work is careful and scheme-theoretic, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Previous page (4) should read 'v + v' = 0, w + w' = 1, v ∈ Γ O_S^*' (consistent with (4bis) and (9)), not 'v w' = 0, w w' = 1'.
Line 2 'pour les impairs [?] g' is likely 'pour les quadruplets' or similar, i.e. 'for v, w, v', w' satisfying (4)'.
'produits ε1, ε0' is likely 'des éléments/matrices ε1, ε0'.
In (7bis) the conjugation notation ρ^{-1}(ε1) means ρ^{-1}ε1ρ.
